en: 2. Khandhayamaka 2.2 Pavattivāra 2.2.2.
Nirodhavāra (The Chapter on Cessation)
2.2.2.1 Present Chapter (Paccuppannavāra) 2.2.2.1.1 Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) ceases,
does the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) cease for that person?

For those passing away from the realm of non-percipient beings, the aggregate of form ceases, but the aggregate of feeling does not cease for them. For those passing away from the five-aggregate plane, both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling cease.
Or conversely, for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling ceases, does the aggregate of form cease for them?

For those passing away from the formless realm, the aggregate of feeling ceases, but the aggregate of form does not cease for them. For those passing away from the five-aggregate plane, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form cease.
2.2.2.1.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa) Where the aggregate of form ceases, does the aggregate of feeling cease there?

In the non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), the aggregate of form (*rūpakkhandha*) ceases there, but the aggregate of feeling (*vedanākkhandha*) does not cease there. In the five-aggregate realm (*pañcavokāra*), both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling cease there.
Or, conversely, where the aggregate of feeling ceases, does the aggregate of form cease there?

In the immaterial realm (*arūpa*), the aggregate of feeling ceases there, but the aggregate of form does not cease there. In the five-aggregate realm, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form cease there.
2.2.2.1.3. Positive Person-Space (Anulomapuggalokāsa) In whom, and where, does the aggregate of form cease, while the aggregate of feeling ceases for that same person in that same place?
For those passing away from the realm of non-percipient beings, the aggregate of form ceases there, but the aggregate of feeling does not cease for them there.
It ceases. For those passing away from the five-aggregate realm, both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling cease there.
Or rather: for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling ceases there, does the aggregate of form cease there for them?
For those passing away from the immaterial realm, the aggregate of feeling ceases there, but the aggregate of form does not cease there for them.
It ceases. For those passing away from the five-aggregate plane, both the feeling aggregate and the form aggregate cease there.
2.2.2.1.4. Negative Person:
For whom the form aggregate does not cease, does the feeling aggregate not cease for that person?
For those passing away from the formless realm, the aggregate of material form does not cease, but the aggregate of feeling does not fail to cease for them.

For all those being reborn, neither the aggregate of material form nor the aggregate of feeling ceases. Or, conversely, for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling does not cease, does the aggregate of material form not cease for them?

For those passing away from the realm of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), the aggregate of feeling (*vedanākkhandha*) does not cease, but the aggregate of form (*rūpakkhandha*) does not fail to cease for them.
For all those being reborn, neither the aggregate of feeling nor the aggregate of form ceases.
2.2.2.1.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where the aggregate of form does not cease, does the aggregate of feeling not cease there? It ceases.
Or else, where the aggregate of feeling does not cease, does the aggregate of form not cease there? It ceases.
2.2.2.1.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa)
For whom the aggregate of form does not cease at a certain place, for them the aggregate of feeling does not cease at that place?
For those passing away from the formless realm, the aggregate of form does not cease there, but it is not the case that the aggregate of feeling does not cease for them there.
For all those being reborn, neither the aggregate of form nor [the aggregate of feeling] ceases there.
And the feeling aggregate does not cease.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever the feeling aggregate does not cease, does the form aggregate not cease for them there?
For those passing away from the non-percipient beings, the feeling aggregate does not cease there, but the form aggregate does not [necessarily] cease for them there.
The aggregate of form does not cease. For all those who are being reborn, there neither the aggregate of feeling nor the aggregate of form ceases at that place.
2.2.2.2. Chapter on the Past.
2.2.2.2.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) had ceased, for that person had the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) ceased? Yes.
Or rather, for whom the aggregate of feeling had ceased, for that person had the aggregate of form ceased? Yes.
2.2.2.2.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where the aggregate of form has ceased, has the aggregate of feeling ceased there?

In the case of non-percipient beings, the aggregate of form has ceased there, but the aggregate of feeling has not ceased there. In the fivefold plane of existence, both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling have ceased there.
Or, where the aggregate of feeling has ceased, has the aggregate of form ceased there?

In the immaterial realm, the aggregate of feeling has ceased there, but the aggregate of form has not ceased there. In the five-aggregate realm, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form have ceased there.
2.2.2.2.3. Positive Correlation: Person and Plane.
For whom and where the aggregate of form has ceased, for them has the aggregate of feeling ceased there?
For non-percipient beings, the aggregate of form has ceased there, but the aggregate of feeling has not ceased for them there.
For those of the five-aggregate realm, both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling have ceased there.
Or again, for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling had ceased at a certain place, had the aggregate of form also ceased for them there?
For those non-percipient beings, the aggregate of feeling had ceased there, but the aggregate of form had not ceased for them there.
For those of the five-aggregate realm, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form had ceased there.
2.2.2.2.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) had not ceased, for that person had the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) not ceased? None.
Or else, for whom the aggregate of feeling had not ceased, for that person had the aggregate of form not ceased? None.
2.2.2.2.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa) Where the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) had not ceased, there the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) had not ceased? It had ceased.
Or else, where the aggregate of feeling had not ceased, there the aggregate of form had not ceased? It had ceased.
2.2.2.2.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) For whom, where the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) had not ceased, for them there, the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) had not ceased?
For non-material beings (arūpānaṃ), the aggregate of form had not ceased there, but for them the aggregate of feeling had not [necessarily] ceased there.
It did not cease. For those Pure Abode beings, neither the aggregate of form nor the aggregate of feeling ceased there.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling did not cease there, did the aggregate of form not cease there for them?
For those non-percipient beings, the aggregate of feeling did not cease there, but the aggregate of form did not [fail to] cease there for them either.
It did not cease. For those Pure Abode beings, there neither ceased the aggregate of feeling nor did the aggregate of form cease there.
2.2.2.3. Chapter on the Future. 2.2.2.3.1.
Positive Person.
For whom the aggregate of form will cease, for that person will the aggregate of feeling cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom the aggregate of feeling will cease, for that person will the aggregate of form cease?
For those who are final-existence beings (pacchimabhavika) reborn in the formless realm, and for those who, having been reborn in the formless realm, will attain final Nibbāna there.
For those who are passing away, the aggregate of feeling will cease, but the aggregate of form will not cease for them.
For others, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form will cease.
2.2.2.3.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Where the aggregate of form will cease, will the aggregate of feeling cease there?

In the case of non-percipient beings, the aggregate of form will cease there, but the aggregate of feeling will not cease there. In the fivefold plane of existence, both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling will cease there.
Or, conversely, where the aggregate of feeling will cease, will the aggregate of form cease there?

In the formless realm (*arūpa*), the aggregate of feeling (*vedanā-khandha*) will cease there, but the aggregate of form (*rūpa-khandha*) will not cease there. In the five-aggregate realm (*pañcavokāra*), both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form will cease there.
2.2.2.3.3. Positive Correlation of Person and Plane:
For whom, wherever the aggregate of form will cease, will the aggregate of feeling cease for that person there?
For non-percipient beings, the aggregate of form will cease there, but the aggregate of feeling will not cease for them there.
For those of the five-aggregate realm, both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling will cease there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling will cease there, will the aggregate of form also cease for them there?
For those immaterial beings, the aggregate of feeling will cease there, but the aggregate of form will not cease for them there.
For those of the five-aggregate realm, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form will cease there.
2.2.2.3.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom the aggregate of form will not cease, for them the aggregate of feeling will not cease?
For those beings of the final existence who are being reborn in the immaterial realm, and for those who, having been reborn in the immaterial realm, will attain final nibbāna at the moment of death—
for them the aggregate of form will not cease, but for them the aggregate of feeling [will cease].
It will not cease. For those who are attaining final Nibbāna, neither the aggregate of form nor the aggregate of feeling will cease.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling will not cease, will the aggregate of form not cease for them? Yes.
2.2.2.3.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa) Where the aggregate of form will not cease, will the aggregate of feeling not cease there? It will cease.
Or else, where the aggregate of feeling will not cease, will the aggregate of form not cease there? It will cease.
2.2.2.3.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) For whom, where the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) will not cease, for them there, will the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) not cease?
For those non-percipient beings (arūpa), the aggregate of form will not cease there, but it is not the case that for them the aggregate of feeling will not cease there.
It will not cease. For those attaining final Nibbāna, there both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling will not cease.
Or rather: for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling will not cease at a certain place, will the aggregate of form also not cease for that person at that place?
For non-percipient beings, the aggregate of feeling will not cease there, but the aggregate of form will not fail to cease for them there.
For those attaining final Nibbāna, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form will not cease there.
2.2.2.4. Chapter on the Present and the Past (Paccuppannātītavāra) 2.2.2.4.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) ceases, for that person has the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) ceased? Yes.
Or again, for whom the aggregate of feeling has ceased, does the aggregate of form cease for them?
For all those being reborn and for those passing away from the formless realm, the aggregate of feeling has ceased, but the aggregate of form does not cease for them.
For those passing away from the five-aggregate plane and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings...
The aggregate of feeling has ceased and the aggregate of form is ceasing.
For whom the aggregate of feeling has ceased, has the aggregate of perception ceased for that person? Yes.
Or rather, for whom the aggregate of perception has ceased, is the aggregate of feeling ceasing for that person?
For all those being reborn and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings, the aggregate of perception has ceased,
but the aggregate of feeling does not cease for them. For those passing away from the four-constituent or five-constituent realms,
both the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of feeling have ceased.
2.2.2.4.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa) Where the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) ceases, has the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) ceased there?

In the case of non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), the aggregate of form ceases there, but the aggregate of feeling has not ceased there. In the five-aggregate plane (pañcavokāra), both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling cease there.
Or, where the aggregate of feeling has ceased, does the aggregate of form cease there?

In the immaterial plane, the aggregate of feeling has ceased there, but the aggregate of form does not cease there. In the five-aggregate plane, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form have ceased.
Where the aggregate of feeling ceases, has the aggregate of perception ceased there? Yes.
Or, where the aggregate of perception has ceased, does the aggregate of feeling cease there? Yes.
2.2.2.4.3. Positive Person-Space:
For whom, wherever the aggregate of form ceases, has the aggregate of feeling ceased there?
For those attaining final nibbāna in the Pure Abodes and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings, the aggregate of material form ceases there,
but the aggregate of feeling has not ceased there for them. For others passing away from the five-aggregate plane,
both the aggregate of material form and the aggregate of feeling cease there.
Or conversely: for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling has ceased at a certain place, does the aggregate of form cease for them there?

For those who are being reborn in the five-aggregate realm and for those non-percipient beings, the aggregate of feeling has ceased there, but the aggregate of form does not cease for them there. For those passing away from the five-aggregate realm, the aggregate of feeling...
And the aggregate of form has ceased.
For whom, where the aggregate of feeling ceases, for them there has the aggregate of perception ceased there?
For those attaining final Nibbāna in the Pure Abodes, the aggregate of feeling ceases there, but for them the aggregate of perception has not [previously] ceased there.
The aggregate of perception had ceased. For those passing away from the four- or five-aggregate planes, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of perception cease there.
Or else, for whomsoever the aggregate of perception had ceased in a certain place, does the aggregate of feeling cease for that person in that same place?
For those being reborn in the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms, the aggregate of perception has ceased there,
but the aggregate of feeling does not cease there for them. For those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms,
both the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of feeling have ceased there.
2.2.2.4.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) does not cease, for that person has the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) not ceased? It has ceased.
Or rather, for whom the aggregate of feeling has not ceased, for that person does the aggregate of form not cease? There is none.
For whom the aggregate of feeling does not cease, for that person has the aggregate of perception not ceased? It has ceased.
Or rather, for whom the aggregate of perception has not ceased, for that person does the aggregate of feeling not cease? There is none.
2.2.2.4.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa).
Where the aggregate of form does not cease (*yattha rūpakkhandho na nirujjhati*—the section [of the formula] should be completed).
2.2.2.4.6. Negative Person-Location:
For whom, where the aggregate of form does not cease, has the aggregate of feeling ceased there?
For those being reborn in the five-aggregate realm and for those in the formless realm, the aggregate of material form does not cease there,
yet the aggregate of feeling has not failed to cease for them there. For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes and for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings,
neither the aggregate of material form nor the aggregate of feeling has ceased there.
Or conversely: for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling has not ceased at a certain place, does the aggregate of form not cease for them there?

For those passing away from the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), the aggregate of feeling has not ceased there, but it is not the case that the aggregate of form does not cease for them there. [This is so] for those being reborn in the Pure Abodes.

For those beings being reborn among the non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), the aggregate of feeling (*vedanākkhandha*) had not ceased there, and the aggregate of form (*rūpakkhandha*) does not cease there.
For whomsoever the aggregate of feeling does not cease there, for that person has the aggregate of perception (*saññākkhandha*) not ceased there?
For those beings being reborn in the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms, the aggregate of feeling does not cease there.

And yet, for them, the aggregate of perception had not ceased there. For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes and for non-percipient beings, neither the aggregate of feeling nor the aggregate of perception has ceased there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever the aggregate of perception had not ceased there, does the aggregate of feeling not cease for them there?
For those attaining final nibbāna in the Pure Abodes, the aggregate of perception has not ceased there,
but the aggregate of feeling does not fail to cease there for them. For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes and for non-percipient beings,
neither the aggregate of perception nor the aggregate of feeling has ceased there.
2.2.2.5. Chapter on the Present and Future (Paccuppannānāgatavāra) 2.2.2.5.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) ceases, will the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) cease for that person?
For those attaining final nibbāna in the five-aggregate plane, the aggregate of material form ceases, but the aggregate of feeling will not cease for them.
For others passing away from the five-aggregate plane and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings,
both the aggregate of material form and the aggregate of feeling will cease.
Or again, for whom the aggregate of feeling will cease, does the aggregate of form cease for them?
For all those who are being reborn and for those passing away from the immaterial realm, the aggregate of feeling will cease, but the aggregate of form does not cease for them.
For those passing away from the five-aggregate plane and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings...
The aggregate of feeling will cease and the aggregate of form ceases.
For whom the aggregate of feeling ceases, will the aggregate of perception cease for them?
For those who are attaining final Nibbāna, the aggregate of feeling ceases, but the aggregate of perception will not cease for them.
For others—those passing away from the four-constituent or five-constituent realms—the aggregate of feeling ceases and the aggregate of perception will also cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever the aggregate of perception will cease, does the aggregate of feeling cease for them?
For all those being reborn and for those passing away from the realm of non-percipient beings, the aggregate of perception will cease.

And yet, their aggregate of feeling does not cease. For those passing away from the four-constituent or five-constituent states, both the aggregate of perception will cease and the aggregate of feeling ceases.
2.2.2.5.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Where the aggregate of form ceases … [etc.
… 2.2.2.5.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa):
For whom, where the aggregate of form ceases, will the aggregate of feeling cease there?
For those attaining final nibbāna in the five-aggregate plane and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings,

the aggregate of form ceases there, but the aggregate of feeling will not cease there for them. For others passing away from the five-aggregate plane, both the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling cease there.
Or conversely: for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling will cease at a certain place, does the aggregate of form cease for them at that same place?

For those beings who are being reborn in the five-aggregate realm and for those non-percipient beings, the aggregate of feeling will cease there, but the aggregate of form does not cease for them there. For those passing away from the five-aggregate realm, the aggregate of feeling...
And the aggregate of form will cease and the aggregate of form is ceasing.
For whomsoever, wherever, the aggregate of feeling ceases, for that person there, will the aggregate of perception cease?
For those who are attaining final Nibbāna, the aggregate of feeling ceases there, but for them the aggregate of perception does not [cease there].
It will cease. For those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of perception cease there.
Or rather, for whomsoever the aggregate of perception will cease in a certain place, does the aggregate of feeling cease for that person in that same place?
For those being reborn in the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms, the aggregate of perception will cease there,
but the aggregate of feeling does not cease for them there. For those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms,
both the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of feeling will cease there.
2.2.2.5.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom the aggregate of form does not cease, will the aggregate of feeling not cease for them?

For all those who are being reborn and for those passing away from the formless realm, the aggregate of form does not cease; yet it is not [the case that] the aggregate of feeling will not cease for them.
For them, the aggregate of feeling will not cease. For those attaining final nibbāna in the formless realm, neither the aggregate of material form nor the aggregate of feeling ceases. Or conversely:
for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling will not cease, does the aggregate of material form not cease for them?
For those attaining final nibbāna in the five-aggregate plane, the aggregate of feeling will not cease, but the aggregate of form does not fail to cease for them.
For those attaining final nibbāna in the immaterial plane, both the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of form will not cease.
For whom the aggregate of feeling does not cease, will the aggregate of perception not cease for them? It will cease.
Or, for whom the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha) will not cease, does the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) not cease for that person? It ceases.
2.2.2.5.5. Negative Spatial Analysis: Where the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) does not cease... [and so forth].
2.2.2.5.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) For whom, where the aggregate of form does not cease, will the aggregate of feeling not cease there for them?
For those being reborn in the five-aggregate realm and for those non-percipient beings, the aggregate of form does not cease there; [but the aggregate of feeling will not cease]. No.

And for them, the feeling aggregate will not cease there. For those attaining final nibbāna in the formless realm and for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings, the material aggregate does not cease there and the feeling aggregate will not cease there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever the feeling aggregate will not cease there, does the material aggregate not cease there for him?
For those attaining final nibbāna in the five-aggregate plane and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings,

the aggregate of feeling will not cease there, but the aggregate of form does not fail to cease for them there. For those attaining final nibbāna in the immaterial plane and for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings, neither the aggregate of feeling nor the aggregate of form will cease there.
For whom the aggregate of feeling does not cease at a certain place, will the aggregate of perception not cease for them at that same place?

For those beings who are being reborn in the four- or five-aggregate realms, the aggregate of feeling does not cease there, yet it is not the case that the aggregate of perception will not cease for them there. For non-percipient beings, the aggregate of feeling...
The aggregate of perception does not cease, and the aggregate of perception will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever the aggregate of perception will not cease at a certain place, does the aggregate of feeling not cease for them there?
For those who are attaining final Nibbāna, the aggregate of perception will not cease there, but the aggregate of feeling does not [not] cease for them there.
It does not cease. For those non-percipient beings, there the aggregate of perception will not cease, and the aggregate of feeling does not cease.
2.2.2.6. Chapter on the Past and Future.
2.2.2.6.1. Positive Person.
For whom the aggregate of form has ceased, will the aggregate of feeling cease for them?

For those who are attaining final Nibbāna, the aggregate of form has ceased, but the aggregate of feeling will not cease for them. For others, both the aggregate of form has ceased and the aggregate of feeling will cease.
Or, for whom the aggregate of feeling will cease, has the aggregate of form ceased for them? Yes.
For whom the aggregate of feeling has ceased, will the aggregate of perception cease for them?

For those who are attaining final Nibbāna, the aggregate of feeling has ceased, but the aggregate of perception will not cease for them. For others, both the aggregate of feeling has ceased and the aggregate of perception will cease.
Or conversely, for whom the aggregate of perception will cease, has the aggregate of feeling ceased for them? Yes.
2.2.2.6.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Wherein the aggregate of form has ceased … pe … 2.2.2.6.3.
Positive Person-Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom, wherever the aggregate of form has ceased, will the aggregate of feeling cease there for them?

For those who are attaining final nibbāna in the five-aggregate realm and for non-percipient beings, the aggregate of form has ceased there, but the aggregate of feeling will not cease there for them.
For others in the five-aggregate realm, [the aggregate of feeling will cease there].
The aggregate of form has ceased and the aggregate of feeling will cease.
Or, for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling will cease at a certain place, has the aggregate of form ceased for them at that same place?
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes and for those non-percipient beings, the aggregate of feeling will cease there, but the aggregate of form has not ceased.
And for those [beings], the aggregate of form had ceased there. For other beings of the five-aggregate realm, both the aggregate of feeling will cease and the aggregate of form had ceased there.
For whomsoever the aggregate of feeling had ceased there, will the aggregate of perception cease there for that person?
For those attaining final nibbāna there, the aggregate of feeling has ceased, but the aggregate of perception will not cease there for them.
For others— those of the four-constituent and five-constituent beings— the aggregate of feeling has ceased there,
and the aggregate of perception will also cease there.
Or again, for whomsoever the aggregate of perception will cease at a certain place, has the aggregate of feeling ceased for them there?
For those beings being reborn in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), the aggregate of perception will cease there, but the aggregate of feeling has not ceased for them there.
For others—those belonging to the four-constituent and five-constituent realms—the [aggregate of perception will cease].
The aggregate of perception will cease and the aggregate of feeling has ceased.
2.2.2.6.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala):
For whom the aggregate of form has not ceased, will the aggregate of feeling not cease for them? None.
Or, for whom the aggregate of feeling will not cease, had the aggregate of form not ceased for them? It had ceased.
For whom the aggregate of feeling had not ceased, will the aggregate of perception not cease for them? There is none.
Or, for whom the aggregate of perception will not cease, had the aggregate of feeling not ceased for them? It had ceased.
2.2.2.6.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where the aggregate of form did not cease …pe… 2.2.2.6.6.
Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom the aggregate of form has not ceased at a certain place, will the aggregate of feeling not cease for them at that same place?

For those who are being reborn in the Pure Abodes and for those in the formless realm, the aggregate of form has not ceased there, yet it is not the case that the aggregate of feeling will not cease for them there. [This is so] for those attaining final nibbāna in the Pure Abodes and for those in the formless realm.
For those attaining final nibbāna there, the aggregate of form has not ceased, and the aggregate of feeling will not cease.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever the aggregate of feeling will not cease there, has the aggregate of form not ceased for them there?
For those attaining final nibbāna in the five-aggregate realm and for non-percipient beings, the aggregate of feeling will not cease there.

And yet, for them, the aggregate of form had not ceased there. For those attaining final nibbāna in the Pure Abodes and those attaining final nibbāna in the formless realm, neither will the aggregate of feeling cease there nor had the aggregate of form ceased there.
For whomsoever the aggregate of feeling had not ceased at a certain place, will the aggregate of perception not cease for him there?
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes, the aggregate of feeling has not ceased there,
yet the aggregate of perception will not fail to cease for them there. For those attaining final nibbāna in the Pure Abodes and for non-percipient beings,
neither the aggregate of feeling nor the aggregate of perception has ceased, nor will the aggregate of perception cease, there.
Or again, for whom the aggregate of perception will not cease at a certain place, has the aggregate of feeling not ceased for them at that place?
For those who are attaining final Nibbāna there, the aggregate of perception will not cease, but it is not the case that the aggregate of feeling has not ceased for them there.
For those attaining final Nibbāna in the Pure Abodes and for non-percipient beings, the aggregate of perception...
And the aggregate of feeling will not cease, and the aggregate of feeling has not ceased.
The section on cessation.
